title: McKinsey research shows AI creating more jobs than automation displaces — but 11 million American workers will need help this decade
source_used: Fortune commentary by McKinsey's Eric Kutcher and Tanguy Catlin (fortune.com page; same text on Yahoo Finance)
key_facts: McKinsey senior partners Eric Kutcher (chair, North America) and Tanguy Catlin (director of the McKinsey Global Institute) write in a Fortune commentary that their new research finds the US economy will have more jobs by 2035 than today, but with a different mix.
Roughly 11 million Americans may need to leave a shrinking occupation for an entirely different one.
An average of 770,000 workers a year will need to cross occupational lines over the next decade, 3.6 times the historical rate.
Automation could take on 80% of hours worked in office and administrative support, the group facing the largest job losses by 2035.
Credentials are required in 85% of growing jobs; about 38% are mandated by law and another 47% reflect employer preferences.
Postings demanding AI fluency have risen elevenfold since 2022, and more than 70% of workers will need new skills even if they never change employers.
The authors urge employers to hire on skills, states to prune licensing rules, and governments to subsidise retraining.
quote_evidence: Our new research finds that the U.S. economy will have more jobs by 2035 than today.
Roughly 11 million Americans may need to leave a shrinking occupation for an entirely different one.
Nearly half the credential problem is a hiring convention rather than a safety rule
why_it_matters_hint: McKinsey projects a reshuffled rather than shrunken US job market, with the main barrier being retraining and credentials.
event_date: 11 Oct 2026 (commentary); research dated 'September' in an earlier CBS account
notes: Opinion commentary by McKinsey's own researchers about McKinsey's own research; no outside check reported. The same 11 million figure was cited in our 5 Oct 2026 edition (CBS 60 Minutes item) from a 'September McKinsey Global Institute report'; the exact date of the research is not given, so freshness points to 4 Oct 2026, the date of that broadcast. The headline claim that AI creates more jobs than it displaces is the headline's framing; the text says the economy will have more jobs by 2035 than today.
